newsitem.title: USA: Dow lower at midday, once again worried on rates.
newsitem.headline: Dow lower at midday, once again worried on rates.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks were having another bad day at mid-session on Thursday, dragged lower by fears of an interest rate hike and falling bonds. But high-tech stocks were back in the limelight.
The Dow Industrials slipped after the opening and were off 25 to 5852 at midday. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index was off one to 681.

The release of several reports of economic data, including strong housing starts, the highest since March of 1994, and lower-than-expected jobless claims lent even more credence to expectations the Federal Reserve would raise rates at its meeting next Tuesday.

"The market had previously had that big unexpected gain, but with the release of the report on Tuesday morning (that the Fed was more seriously considering a rate hike), the music stopped," said Prudential analyst Larry Wachtel. "Now there is a kernel of doubt about what will happen at the Fed meeting, so the sense is to sit on your assets, why get in trouble?"
"With the higher-than-expected housing starts and the Yom Kippur holiday Monday, people are sitting it out," he said.

Cowen & Co market analyst Charles Pradillo said, "There are other things going on today, too -- triple witching (the expiration of options) is tommorow, and window-dressing by portfolio managers, so we're in very choppy territory".

High-technology stocks defied the broader drop. A bullish forecast by Intel Corp about company profits and the industry in general released late Monday has turned the spotlight back on tech stocks, which have been rising steadily since.
In special situations today, three initial public offerings were the highest-flying stocks on the Nasdaq.

Cymer Corp shares jumped 42 percent. The company makes excimer lasers for deep ultraviolet photolithography systems, which make the very small images used in manufacturing advanced semiconductor chips. Shares of the San Diego company rose 3-7/8 to 13-3/8.
Rental Services Corp RSCV.O, which rents out pumps, generators, forklifts and other industrial equipment, rose 5-1/4 to 21-1/4, or 32 percent at its market debut.
